scope: Partial recovered contract for the original object keyword handler, model lifecycle, scanners and selected runtime imports. Static and runtime evidence are recorded separately; this is not a complete model specification.

syntax_corroboration.description: Previously captured original KEY export contains OBJNAM object-id followed by name line, OBJTYP object-id type-code secondary-code, RZ object-id node-count followed by labeled coordinate rows, and ELMCON object-id element-count arity followed by labeled connectivity rows.
syntax_corroboration.limitation: Export syntax does not independently prove the import table's numeric keyword assignments or its tolerance rules.

facts: Except keyword ID 0x11e, the handler first calls fscanf with %i into an object-ID temporary and then 0x14019ccc0(application, object-ID).
Only fscanf result -1 is explicitly rejected at this call site; complete malformed-token behavior depends on the scanner and previous/local values.
A null returned object leads to status 2.

Companion analysis of 0x14019ccc0 returns null for IDs less than1; otherwise finds an existing object through0x14017aaf0. When absent, appends intermediate placeholder objects of internal type7 up to the requested ID, then creates the requested object and updates application+0x1378.

New requested objects initialize internal type0, empty name, no mesh, zero node/element counts and, in 3D, element kind2/arity4. Intermediate placeholders override internal type to7. Remaining defaults and ownership come from many constructor subobjects and remain only partly mapped.
Switch case0 invokes 0x140413ab0(FILE, object+0x828, 0x51). The destination matches the DB-import name field.
The helper consumes the remainder of the keyword line with one fgets, then reads the following line with a second fgets. Either EOF returns failure1 without copying the name.
It replaces the first LF with NUL, copies at most80 bytes using strncpy, scans backward from byte79 ignoring NUL, space, LF and CR, then terminates after the final retained byte.
Leading whitespace is retained. Trailing tabs are not included in its trim set. An all-space/CR/LF or empty name becomes empty. Bytes after the first NUL are not meaningful string content.
This proves an80-byte import name limit for this call, wider than the64-byte name storage observed in the DB descriptor; the two formats must not be assigned one guessed name limit.

Reads two integers through 0x140413ee0 before applying the type mapping. The helper zeroes both outputs, reads one line, replaces commas with spaces, and treats sscanf conversion count 0 or 1 as success; only EOF(-1) is rejected. A nonnumeric first token can therefore produce type0 rather than an import error.
Writes internal type at object+0xc: file 1->0, 2->1, 3->2, 4->3, 5->4, and 7->6.
File type 6 leaves the previous internal type unchanged in this branch.
Other file types set internal type 7.
The second integer is stored at object+0x2154.

If the resulting internal type is 7, calls 0x140161260(object). Companion analysis shows it clears the name, mesh flag, node/element counts and other fields, iterates100 per-object subrecords, and calls deeper cleanup0x14015fbf0. The complete cleanup scope is still unresolved.
Reads a count through 0x140413de0, then immediately writes it to object+0x880.

Calls 0x1401652b0(object, count, application+0x15f8) before reading rows. That callee calls0x140162ff0, then initializes the double array at object+0x8e0 to20.0 or68.0 according to0x140235c10 and a component-count field. Thus repeated coordinate import affects a dependent field too; its precise domain meaning is not asserted here.

Allocation proceeds through 0x140162ff0: first 0x140163270(object), then 0x14017ffe0(object+0x8a0,node-count,component-table,-1). Cleanup 0x14017f130 frees and nulls coordinates and several auxiliary arrays, resets stored counts and invokes generic cleanup 0x140329dc0. Positive-count allocation uses calloc-backed helpers and then generic 0x140329e60; previous coordinate contents are not preserved.
The coordinate pointer is object+0x8a8.
When 0x1400015e0(application) returns zero, each row is parsed through 0x140415880 into one temporary row label and three consecutive 8-byte coordinate slots.
The other branch calls 0x140415680 for a temporary label and two consecutive 8-byte coordinate slots.
Destination indices come from the sequential loop counter. The parsed row label is not used to select the destination in this handler.
Each nonzero row-reader status returns 2 immediately. The count and any earlier rows have already been changed; no rollback is present at this level.
This branch does not explicitly set the mesh-present field at object+0x87c.
The3D row helper0x140415880 zeroes label and all three double outputs before reading, reads one line up to1023 bytes, replaces commas with spaces, and parses %i plus three %Flf conversions.

It treats any sscanf return other than-1 as success, so a short or malformed nonblank row may leave zero-filled missing components without reporting failure. This is static behavior; all numeric grammar edge cases are not runtime-verified.
In the three-coordinate branch, reads element count and arity through 0x140413ee0.
Arity 4 calls 0x140165500(object,2); arity 8 calls 0x140165500(object,4); other arities return 2 before storing the new count.
In the other dimension branch, reads only the count through 0x140413de0.

Writes element count at object+0x884, then calls 0x1401653b0(object, count, application+0x15f8). That callee resets dependent arrays: object+0xa30 doubles to1.0, object+0xa38 doubles to0.0, and conditionally object+0x9f8 integer entries from object+0x3980.

Allocation proceeds through 0x140163090: first 0x1401632a0(object), then 0x1401836c0(object+0x9e0,count,component-table,arity,-1). Cleanup 0x140182a50 frees and nulls connectivity and two auxiliary arrays, resets stored count/arity and invokes generic cleanup 0x140329dc0. Positive-count connectivity and auxiliary integer allocation uses calloc-backed helpers, then generic 0x140329e60.
Generic field allocation/cleanup and domain meanings of the dependent arrays remain incompletely mapped; the explicit connectivity replacement and zero-initialization are established.
Connectivity pointer is object+0x9e8. Selection between 4 and 8 integers per row uses internal element-kind field object+0x890.
Rows are read through 0x140414200 for label plus four integers, or 0x140414600 for label plus eight integers.
Parsed row labels are temporary. Destination is sequential row index, independent of the label in this handler.
A row-reader failure returns 2 after count, type and possibly preceding rows have already changed.
After all rows succeed, sets object+0x87c to 1.
Calls 0x14039aa20(application), then calls 0x1401fc290(object) when that predicate is zero; the postprocessing semantics remain unresolved.

0x140165500 writes element-kind at+0x890. Kind2 sets+0x894=4,+0x898=4,+0x89c=3; kind4 sets8,6,4 respectively. Only the first value is directly proven here as connectivity arity; the other two domain meanings are inferred from topology, not named source fields.

The4-node row helper0x140414200 zeroes all five integer outputs, reads one line (optionally skips LF-only blank lines under its last parameter), replaces commas with spaces, and parses five %i fields. Only sscanf return-1 is failure; incomplete or malformed nonblank rows may succeed with zero remainder.
The ELMCON call sites shown pass a zero skip-blank flag for four-node rows.

Fresh static evidence in analysis/model-0x140414600.json (ev_4f99c41662703985b0ba14f4f334e9a5d69f12302acafa0bf85d0429837b8af2) establishes the eight-node helper: zero all nine integer outputs, read at most 1023 bytes with fgets, optionally skip LF-only empty lines, replace commas with spaces, scan nine %i fields and return failure only when fgets fails or sscanf returns -1. Zero or partial conversions therefore leave zero-filled output suffixes and report success.

The eight-node helper's malformed-row and numeric-grammar behavior is statically recovered, not yet established by a dedicated runtime grammar matrix. Decimal-only strict parsing must not be substituted silently for the original %i scanner.
The parser consumes keyword tokens sequentially and dispatches immediately; it has no visible duplicate-keyword rejection or deferred all-file transaction.
Handlers write directly into application/object fields. Repeated scalar/name/type keywords can overwrite earlier state, subject to individual branch rules.
Repeated coordinate/connectivity blocks free and replace their primary arrays, allocate zero-initialized storage, and reset dependent fields. The full dependent-field list still requires recovery.
Object-handler success is returned as 0; nonzero local reader status is generally normalized to 2.
Parser status 2 prints a reading-error message and resumes token scanning; status 3 prints a data-error message and resumes scanning. Other nonzero handler statuses exit the parser.
The parser remembers an earlier nonzero status and can return it at EOF even if later records succeeded.
Malformed multi-line input can leave a partially changed object and subsequent tokens may be interpreted as keywords. Exact resulting state requires runtime tests.
The wrapper closes the file and, when its caller-supplied flag is true, calls finalization even when the parser returns an error. No rollback is visible in that wrapper.

Object-list append0x14017a880 allocates0x3f28 bytes, constructs through0x14015ec80, updates head/tail, and links successive objects at object+0x3940. This records physical original layout, not a requirement to reproduce it in modern C++.
The object initializer0x14015f0b0 initializes separate node, element and other subobjects and allocates100 subrecords of0x130 bytes. Many of their meanings and lifecycle dependencies remain unknown.

Before data-category dispatch, parser calls0x1401d81b0. If application+0x33e8 is nonnull and+0x33f0 is nonzero, that helper selects an alternate application pointer. Otherwise it returns the original pointer.
Thus all keyword categories cannot yet be assumed to mutate only one global root; the alternate-context purpose and synchronization are unresolved.
Direct table inspection confirms 304 rows at 0x140544400 with 48-byte stride; selected strings and entries were read completely.
Object category2 mappings: OBJNAM ID144, OBJTYP ID145, RZ ID159, ELMCON ID173.
Command category6 mappings include DBREAD ID2, KFREAD ID3 and GENDB ID4. Reading a keyword file can therefore invoke command behavior, not only data assignment.
Lookup 0x1402f78d0 uses case-sensitive strcmp. Runtime lowercase objtyp was unresolved while uppercase OBJNAM was recognized.

next_procedures.question: Generic field-array allocation policy and component-table meanings.
Generic field-array cleanup and ownership, beyond explicitly freed primary arrays.
Full inactive/unsupported object cleanup and retained state.
Eight-node connectivity-row scanner and incomplete-field semantics.
Complete finalization invariants, beyond observed name/type/count fields.

limitations: Static observations and controlled runtime observations are separated; neither establishes complete importer/model semantics.
OBJNAM, OBJTYP, RZ and ELMCON spelling/ID/category mappings are confirmed by direct table inspection and runtime resolution.
Decompiler signatures and local types may be inaccurate; field stores and pointer widths are evidence, not recovered original C++ declarations.
No claims cover all model fields, every keyword, complete ownership or all allocation/finalization effects.
No C++ model or importer was implemented from these partial observations.

runtime_observations.scope: Seven sequential imports in one original-app process, containing six distinct small fixtures. Hooks observe selected fields; no mesh was loaded in this run. Completed exit0 with unchanged input hashes.

findings.fact: First import created object1. Immediately after creation it had internal type0, empty C string, mesh0, counts0, kind2 and arity4; OBJTYP changed it to1 and OBJNAM set REA baseline object.
A name-only subsequent import reused the same object and preserved its internal type1 and counts while replacing name with REA renamed object.
Reimporting baseline reused the existing object and restored its name; object/list counts stayed1.
Repeated names applied in input order; the second name remained. A later type keyword changed type to0 while preserving that name.
Name before type worked for an already-existing object. This run does not establish the same ordering on a fresh object.
REA_UNKNOWN_TEST resolved to sentinel305; parser continued to a later OBJNAM, and import returned0.
OBJTYP 1 BAD 0 returned handler status0, changed internal type to7 and cleared the name. A following OBJNAM updated the same inactive object; final import status was0.

Finalization was called for every completed import. Selected observed identity/type/name/count fields were unchanged across these finalizations; this does not establish that unobserved fields were unchanged.

limitations: Probe captured65 name bytes, so runtime evidence does not verify80-byte maximum or complete tail storage.
Raw bytes after NUL contain uninitialized or previous storage and must not be interpreted as part of the name.
No reset/merge guarantee is established for all other keyword categories or alternate contexts.
No type6 runtime case is present in this first run.

remaining_architecture_unknowns: Complete application-root constructor/defaults, owned subobjects and lifetime of primary versus alternate root.

Generic field-array ownership, complete dependent-field reset/invalidation policy and its coupling to materials, interactions and derived geometry. Explicit primary coordinate/connectivity free-and-calloc replacement is established.
Full material/object/interaction ownership and reference graph, including coupled2D/3D model contexts.
Invariants and derived values established by each finalization stage; invalid partial models may survive parsing but fail later.
Command keyword effects beyond data assignment, including DBREAD, nested imports, positioning and file generation.
All default-value sources, unit conversions and dimension-dependent behavior.
Difference between active object count, placeholder/list count, model completeness and simulation validity.
Round-trip behavior and losses between DB arrays, application state and KEY export, including64-byte versus80-byte names.
Error propagation and partial updates across every category; no universal transactional assumption is supported.

runtime_observations_mesh.scope: Seven sequential imports in a separate original-app process, containing six distinct fixtures. One four-node tetrahedron plus placeholder/sparse object cases; selected node/element arrays and scalar fields observed.

findings.fact: RZ resolved as159 and ELMCON as173. Baseline produced object1, internal type1, mesh flag1, four nodes, one element, kind2/arity4, expected twelve coordinate components and connectivity [1,2,3,4].
Nonsequential row labels did not change placement: coordinates were stored in input order as [10,0,0,11,0,0,10,1,0,10,0,1] and connectivity remained [1,2,3,4].
Truncated RZ returned import status2 but retained changed coordinates [20,0,0,21,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0], count4, prior one-element connectivity and mesh flag1. It did not restore the previous valid model.
Finalization still ran after the truncated coordinate import; the selected partial mesh state survived to import return.
Reimporting the baseline restored the tested fields and arrays in the same object record.
OBJNAM for object4 created placeholder records2 and3 of internal type7 and requested record4 of default type0 with the supplied name. Existing tetrahedron object1 remained; object/list count became4.
File type6 left object1 at internal type1, consistent with the static no-assignment branch.
Lowercase objtyp resolved to sentinel305 and was skipped. Following uppercase OBJNAM changed the name, while internal type and mesh remained unchanged; import status0.

The observed dependent arrays after mesh imports contained node array+0x8e0 prefix [20,20,20,20], element array+0xa30 [1], and+0xa38 [0]. Their full domain meanings are not established by these values.

limitations: Only3D four-node tetrahedra and small positive counts were exercised.
No eight-node elements, zero/negative counts, allocation failure or complete material/interaction data was exercised.
Numerical correctness or suitability of the partial model for simulation is not implied by successful finalization.
Pointer reuse does not imply in-place preservation: allocators may reuse freed addresses.
Runtime names are short; the80-byte limit remains a static finding.
